scope.description: Run the shutdown probe for VerifyLeader, Barrier and Apply with the default unbuffered applyCh and for Barrier and Apply with BatchApplyCh enabled, three trials each, recording racing and post-shutdown completion counts and the batch_apply_ch flag, with a no-shutdown control; the batched cases use distinct trial identifiers so each result event is admitted by a single setup event.
assumptions: BatchApplyCh is a supported option whose documented effect is to buffer applyCh to MaxAppendEntries and to break the timeout guarantee on Apply.
MaxAppendEntries (the default) is large enough that the post-shutdown sends never block, so the buffered send stays selectable exactly as verifyCh's does.
Single-voter node, in-memory transport, 50ms timeouts, one process.
excluded: Multi-node behaviour and buffer sizes small enough to block the sends.

basis.prefix: Each case starts one real Raft instance with its own InmemStore, InmemSnapshotStore and InmemTransport, bootstrapped as a single Voter with HeartbeatTimeout = ElectionTimeout = LeaderLeaseTimeout = 50ms and BatchApplyCh set only for the batched cases, and waits until it reports Leader. It emits assurance_shutdown_setup carrying trial, kind, shutdown, batch_apply_ch, the call counts and the window, then issues 128 calls of the chosen kind from separate goroutines, each waiting on Error() with a 4000ms deadline, and in the shutdown cases calls Shutdown() from a goroutine 2ms later. After Shutdown returns it issues 8 further calls one at a time with a 500ms wait each and emits assurance_shutdown_result with the racing counts, the post-phase counts and histograms, the shutdown error, the node state and batch_apply_ch. Batched barrier and apply cases use trial identifiers 100 to 102 so their setup and result events are distinguishable from the unbuffered ones. The harness is TestAssuranceShutdownFutureCompletion.

comparisons.description: Barrier with BatchApplyCh: at least one post-shutdown call left unanswered, which would confirm the strand follows buffering.
Apply with BatchApplyCh: same prediction for the documented buffered configuration.
Barrier with the default unbuffered applyCh: every post-shutdown call answered.
Apply with the default unbuffered applyCh: same contrast.
VerifyLeader, whose channel is always buffered: the strand re-measured alongside the batched cases.

before.description: Run the shutdown probe for VerifyLeader, Barrier and Apply with the default unbuffered applyCh and again for Barrier and Apply with BatchApplyCh enabled, three trials each, recording how many futures are left incomplete in the racing phase and how many of eight post-shutdown calls are answered in the 500ms window, plus a no-shutdown control.
assumptions: BatchApplyCh is a supported configuration option whose documented effect is to buffer applyCh to MaxAppendEntries and to break the timeout guarantee on Apply.
Buffer size is MaxAppendEntries (the default), which is large enough that the eight post-shutdown sends never block, so the send case is selectable exactly as verifyCh's is.
Single-voter node, in-memory transport, 50ms timeouts, one process, as before.
excluded: BatchApplyCh with BatchApplyChMaxAppendEntries or concurrency large enough to fill the buffer, and multi-node behaviour.

revision_reason: The batched cases were admitted ambiguously because they shared trial and kind with the unbuffered cases and the setup event did not carry batch_apply_ch, so their comparisons were unresolved. This revision gives the batched cases trial identifiers 100 to 102 and records batch_apply_ch on the setup event as well as the result event, so each result event can be admitted by exactly one setup event. Cases, event names and measured fields are otherwise unchanged.
